summary: One correction, in two places: the story had mixed up two of Pfungst's tests. When the questioner knew the answer Hans was right 98 per cent of the time, against 8 per cent when they didn't; the 89 and 6 per cent figures come from the blinker test, and Hans did still answer with blinkers on. Everything else checked out.

changes.before: When the person asking knew the answer and Hans could see them, he was right 89 per cent of the time. When they didn't, he was right 6 per cent of the time. With blinkers on, he couldn't answer at all.
changes.after: When the person asking knew the answer, he was right 98 per cent of the time. When they didn't, he was right 8 per cent of the time. With blinkers on, he was right 89 per cent of the time when he could still see the questioner, and 6 per cent when he couldn't.
changes.why: Pfungst reports 98% correct with knowledge (42 tests) and 8% without (49 tests). The 89% and 6% figures are from the blinker test: questioner seen (56 tests) versus not seen (35 tests).

changes.before: When the questioner knew the answer, Hans was right 89 per cent of the time; when they didn't, 6 per cent.
changes.after: When the questioner knew the answer, Hans was right 98 per cent of the time; when they didn't, 8 per cent.
changes.why: Same correction, so the quiz agrees with the story and with Pfungst.

notes: The Horse Journals source makes the same mix-up of the 89 and 6 per cent figures. It still supports the rest of what it's cited for, so I kept it.

history.summary: Published before the fact-checker existed. Waiting for its first check.
